close_reason: Landed in 8d12c8e. All sites where the format arg is a plain binding are now inline-capture: writeln! / format! calls in tests/common/mod.rs, the three bench convert_* closures, and examples/parse_eml.rs:36. The one positional site format!('bnd{}', i + 1) is kept because the arg is an expression (the bead explicitly recommended leaving it).
description:
What the code does: `crate-jmap-mime/benches/mime_pipeline.rs` and `crate-jmap-mime/examples/parse_eml.rs` use the legacy positional `format!("...{}", x)` form in multiple places, including in the closure passed to `message_to_jmap_body` (`Id::from(format!("blob-{}", p.part_id))`).

What idiomatic Rust would do: inline-capture the identifier in the format string — `format!("blob-{part_id}")`. Rust 1.58 stabilised this; the workspace targets a much newer rustc (1.88+ per Cargo.toml `rust-version` inheritance), so there is no MSRV reason to keep the legacy form. Clippy's pedantic `uninlined_format_args` flags every instance.

Why it matters: inline-captured format args are now the unambiguous idiom because (a) they read like Python f-strings or shell interpolation, which is the cognitive model every Rust practitioner since 2022 reads first, (b) they make the arg-to-placeholder correspondence visible at the point of use instead of via positional pairing, which is the source of most format-arg bugs, and (c) they reduce noise (`format!("blob-{part_id}")` vs `format!("blob-{}", part.part_id)` is a measurable readability win when there are multiple args). Two of the four bench-file `format_push_string` sites (lines 88, 185) compound the issue by also being positional — fixing both together is one edit.

Concrete sites (in-scope diff only):
- crate-jmap-mime/benches/mime_pipeline.rs:88 — `format!("Content-ID: <part-{}@example.com>\\r\\n", idx)`
- crate-jmap-mime/benches/mime_pipeline.rs:133 — `format!("bnd{}", i + 1)` (this one has an expression, not just an ident, so inline-capture would need a `let n = i + 1;` first — leave as-is or inline; minor)
- crate-jmap-mime/benches/mime_pipeline.rs:143 — `format!("Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=\"{}\"\\r\\n", boundaries[0])` (subscript, leave positional)
- crate-jmap-mime/benches/mime_pipeline.rs:167 — `format!("Content-ID: <L{}-leaf-{}@example.com>\\r\\n", level + 1, leaf_idx)` (level + 1 is an expression; `leaf_idx` can inline)
- crate-jmap-mime/benches/mime_pipeline.rs:185 — `format!("Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=\"{}\"\\r\\n", inner)` (inner is a binding — straightforward inline)
- crate-jmap-mime/benches/mime_pipeline.rs:299, 312, 325, 340, 353, 366 — six bench-loop closures `Id::from(format!("blob-{}", p.part_id))` (`p.part_id` is a field access; one-step bind-and-inline)
- crate-jmap-mime/examples/parse_eml.rs:36 — `Id::from(format!("blob-{}", part.part_id))` (same pattern)

Out of scope: lib.rs is unchanged in scope. The fix is mechanical and pure noise reduction — pair with t307.11 (`format_push_string`) in one cleanup commit.
title: Bench and example use `format!("...{}", x)` instead of inline-capture `{x}`
